title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
premise: In a Hertfordshire village, Mrs. Bennet has five unmarried daughters and one mission. When a wealthy young bachelor rents the estate nearby, bringing along a proud and aloof friend, Elizabeth Bennet, the sharpest of the sisters, forms her opinions quickly. A comedy of manners about first impressions, and how wrong they can be.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
premise: A restless young man signs on to a whaling ship out of Nantucket and discovers that its captain is hunting something far more personal than oil. Part sea adventure, part encyclopedia of whaling, part philosophical sermon: the great American novel about obsession.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
premise: A young scientist, consumed by the ambition to discover the secret of life, succeeds, and recoils from what he has made. Framed by the letters of an explorer sailing toward the North Pole, the novel Shelley began at eighteen asks what we owe to the things we create.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
premise: Nick Carraway rents a small house on Long Island next to the mansion of Jay Gatsby, a mysterious millionaire famous for his extravagant parties. Over one Jazz Age summer, Nick is drawn into the lives of the rich and restless around him. A short, luminous novel about longing and reinvention.

title: Mrs Dalloway
author: Virginia Woolf
premise: One June day in London, 1923. Clarissa Dalloway walks through the city to buy flowers for the party she is giving that evening. Woolf follows her thoughts, and those of the people around her, as they move freely between the present and memory: a whole life seen through a single day.

title: Middlemarch
author: George Eliot
premise: In a provincial English town around 1830, the idealistic Dorothea Brooke longs to do something great with her life, while a young doctor arrives with plans to reform medicine. Eliot weaves their lives into a portrait of an entire community. Often called the greatest novel in English.

title: Dom Casmurro
author: Machado de Assis
premise: An older man living alone in Rio de Janeiro decides to write his memoirs, to tie together the two ends of his life: his childhood, his first love for Capitu, the girl next door, and what became of them. The narrator is charming, digressive, and not necessarily to be trusted. (Original 1899 spelling.)

title: Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas
author: Machado de Assis
premise: Brás Cubas is dead, and finally free to be honest about his life. Writing from beyond the grave in short, playful, irreverent chapters, a wealthy Rio gentleman recounts his loves, ambitions and failures. The novel that changed Brazilian literature. (Original 1881 spelling.)

title: The Lady with the Dog
author: Anton Chekhov
premise: At the seaside resort of Yalta, a bored, married Moscow banker notices a young woman who walks alone every day with her small white dog. Chekhov's most famous story, and one of the great short stories about love. About 25 minutes to read.

title: The Student
author: Anton Chekhov
premise: On a cold Good Friday evening, a hungry seminary student walks home through the countryside and stops at a fire where two widows are warming themselves. A four-page story, often said to have been Chekhov's own favourite. About 5 minutes to read.

title: Gooseberries
author: Anton Chekhov
premise: Two friends caught in the rain take shelter at a country estate. One of them tells the story of his brother, a clerk who saved all his life for a little farm with a gooseberry bush. A story about happiness, and who pays for it. About 15 minutes to read.

title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
premise: Eight years ago, Anne Elliot was persuaded to break off her engagement to a young naval officer with no fortune. Now he is back, rich and admired, and she is twenty-seven, overlooked by her vain family. Austen's last completed novel, and her most quietly emotional.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
premise: An orphan raised by a cruel aunt grows up plain, poor, and fiercely independent, and takes a post as governess at a remote country house whose master is moody and whose upper floors hold a secret. Told in Jane's own unforgettable voice.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
premise: A gentleman renting a house on the Yorkshire moors meets his strange landlord, Heathcliff, and asks the housekeeper for the story behind him. What she tells is a tale of two families and a passion that refuses to stay buried. Brontë's only novel.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
premise: Pip, an orphan raised by his harsh sister and her gentle blacksmith husband, has two chance encounters, one with an escaped convict and one with a strange rich woman in a decaying house, that change the course of his life. A novel about ambition, gratitude and snobbery.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
premise: In imperial Russian society, two stories unfold side by side: a married woman who falls into a passion that society will not forgive, and an awkward landowner searching for meaning in love, work and faith. Often called the greatest novel ever written.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
premise: In the stifling summer heat of St. Petersburg, a penniless former student convinces himself that some people stand above ordinary morality, and resolves to prove it. A psychological thriller written from inside a feverish mind.

title: Song of Myself
author: Walt Whitman
premise: Whitman's great long poem: a celebration of the self, the body, the grass and the crowd, in which the 'I' who speaks keeps expanding to include everyone. Fifty-two sections; read one or read them all.

title: Crossing Brooklyn Ferry
author: Walt Whitman
premise: Standing on the ferry between Manhattan and Brooklyn at sunset, Whitman speaks directly to the people who will make the same crossing long after he is gone, which means to you.

title: Ode to a Nightingale
author: John Keats
premise: Listening to a nightingale on a spring night, the poet longs to escape with it from a world of sickness and time. Written in 1819, when Keats was twenty-three. Eight stanzas.

title: To Autumn
author: John Keats
premise: Keats's last great poem: three stanzas that move through the season from ripeness, to harvest, to the music of the year's end.

title: Ode on a Grecian Urn
author: John Keats
premise: The poet contemplates the scenes painted on an ancient Greek vase: lovers, musicians, a village procession, all frozen forever in a single moment. Five stanzas.
